The first generation run under the operator directive of 2026-08-28, which fuses operator authority into the loop and replaces the two-party arrangement with a hashed condition ladder (LADDER.md), a self-ruling ledger (RULINGS.md) and an unreachability standard that has to be earned. The close of 2026-08-26 forbade a generation 11; that prohibition was issued by the operator under the arrangement this directive replaces, and the directive's section 8 instructs the next generation's Phase A by name. why_not_terminated: the stopping rule is claim-surface stationarity (directive section 5): two consecutive generations in which every finding is below HIGH, changes no spine item and changes no stated limitation. This generation changed two spine items and removed a limitation, so it is not stationary and the count of consecutive stationary generations is zero.

schema.champion_commit: The last CONTENT commit, by definition. Never the commit that wrote this file: a state file cannot name its own commit, because its bytes are part of the tree that commit hashes. Guarded by tests/test_loop_state_close.py.
schema.bookkeeping_commit: null at write time, always. Nothing may fill this during the commit that writes the file, because the value would be that commit's own hash.
schema.machinery_commit: Equal to champion_commit. The addendum's measurement ran against the working tree that became that commit, byte for byte: the run executed, then the artefacts and the code that produced them were committed together. The distinction the earlier files draw between the tree a measurement ran against and the tree carrying its results does not arise, and each artefact additionally pins its inputs by SHA-256.

open_findings.note: Narrowed once more at close, by arithmetic rather than by measurement. Generation 10 killed the localisation mechanism and left the question 'why is the leading direction fixed while the ones behind it cross the noise floor'. The free check answers the descriptive half: the leading direction is not merely fixed, it is FALLING -- by a factor of 1.195 and 1.148, spearman -1.000 and -0.983 -- which is the wrong direction to raise a count against an absolute cutoff, and the climb is carried entirely by the trailing values rising toward it. 95.6% to 97.9% of each trailing value's motion is in the normalised spectrum. So the phenomenon is the spectrum FLATTENING, and the open question is why widening the bias window compresses the sensitivity spectrum toward its own leading direction. Nothing here answers that and the ruling forbids chasing it. Untouched by the addendum, which measured no spectrum.

open_findings.status: OPEN, AND ITS CONSEQUENCE IS NOW PAID
open_findings.note: Unchanged as a finding; what changed is that its consequence has been taken rather than noted. Every barrier walks a straight line in that chart's own coordinates, so every depth is an UPPER bound. The closing ruling section 3 follows that all the way: it STRENGTHENS the chart-G ridge, whose true barrier is then at most at the floor, and WEAKENS both d=16 results to search statements -- no connecting path below the floor was found along the straight line, which is not separation. The test that would settle it is a minimum-energy path, string method or NEB against the same oracle with the same floor barrier as the criterion. It was not run and is out of budget. AH-13 applies in its usual direction. Untouched by the addendum: refining witnesses does not compute a minimum-energy path, and chart G's recounted median is an upper bound exactly as its predecessor was. The bound direction is what makes the recounted median's fall a strengthening rather than a change of sign.
